title: 210. why you’re feeling suicidal + a therapist’s advice on how to cope feat. kathryn gordon
description_html: Today's guest is Kathryn Gordon— a licensed clinical psychologist, speaker, and author. She specializes in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and has written several books on using CBT skills to prevent suicide.
talk_about: How suicidal thoughts progress into behaviors
What to expect when in therapy for suicidal thoughts
CBT skills that are most effective for suicidal thoughts
Resources for when someone is in a crisis

guests: dr. kathryn gordon, licensed clinical psychologist and author
summary: sadie talks with dr. kathryn gordon, a clinical psychologist specializing in cbt for suicide prevention, about why people have suicidal thoughts and how to cope with them. they cover what prompts suicidal ideation (feeling like a burden, isolated, or in hopeless pain), why it feels impossible to do helpful things when you're struggling, and how to talk about suicide openly without shame. kathryn walks through cbt tools like identifying thought patterns, reframing beliefs, and building a safety plan with distraction skills and environmental changes. she also explains what peers can do to support friends—listen non-judgmentally, encourage professional help, and set boundaries—without taking on responsibility they can't handle.
quote: the goal is to have a plan in place so that when you can't think clearly, you can still access it.
quote_display: the goal is to have a PLAN in place so that when you CAN'T THINK CLEARLY, you can still ACCESS it.
